text:
alice: Heads-up — after the autoscaler rollout we saw oscillations on small tenants. Want a quick sync on mitigation strategies and clear operator vs control-plane boundaries.

ben: Yep, saw lease churn. Tenants hit burst lane, then prewarm gets canceled, then they re-request and we spin up again. Observed ~3x scale events in 5m for some tenants.

carla: I dug into the logs. The admission proxy is aggressively reclaiming soft-reservations once usage dips below a tiny threshold. That plus short lease TTL is the culprit.

ben: Agreed. Two loose knobs we have so far: lease_ttl and burst_credit_decay. Both help but trade latency for cost.

esha: +1. We should avoid ad-hoc knobs if we can define a simple control contract: operator owns short-term stabilizers (hysteresis, short prewarm), control-plane owns committed capacity and accounting.

frank: What do people think about token-banking (save unused burst credit) vs hysteresis (wait before shrinking)? Token-banking is fairer but increases complexity and state.

carla: For small tenants token-bank state per-tenant is cheap, but it complicates rebalancing when nodes are scarce. Hysteresis is stateless and predictable: shrink only if util < X for Y seconds.

alice: My worry with pure hysteresis: it can artificially inflate steady-state headroom and hurt tight clusters. We need a hybrid: hysteresis + ephemeral bank for burst smoothing.

ben: Sketch of hybrid: keep a small ephemeral credit balance per-tenant (decays fast), and require util < shrink_threshold AND credit == 0 to evict. That prevents rapid oscillation but allows cluster to reclaim after credits drain.

carla: sketch pseudocode:
```
# on scale-down decision
if util < SHRINK_THRESH and time_since_last_scale > HYSTERESIS_WINDOW:
  if ephemeral_credit <= 0:
    evict_slot()
  else:
    ephemeral_credit -= shrink_cost
    keep_slot()
```

esha: That looks reasonable. We should define shrink_cost relative to expected burst duration (e.g., one 30s token). Also record lease_age so we avoid thrashing freshly-created slots.

frank: What about operator boundary? If operator manages ephemeral_credit and hysteresis, the control-plane still needs to expose: max_committed, tenant_priority, SLA_tier. Operator uses them to make local choices.

alice: Exactly. Operator contract proposal: the control-plane sends desired_committed and a policy flags bag {allow_burst:true/false, burst_limit:N, prewarm_budget:M}. Operator implements local stabilizers but must never exceed desired_committed + burst_limit without explicit permission.

ben: One important metric we need to emit: scale_decision_reason (hysteresis, credit_exhausted, manual_evict). Makes debugging much easier.

carla: +1 and include lease_provision_ts and last_activity_ts in telemetry. Also add a gauge for ephemeral_credit per-tenant.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of autoscaler v2 to us-west-2 complete :white_check_mark:

alice: Nice. Let's avoid expanding canary until we toggle ephemeral-credit on for 10% of tenants only. Need to validate no new oscillation traces.

esha: Ops checklist suggestion:
- enable ephemeral_credit=on for 10% tenants
- collect scale_decision_reason, lease_age, ephemeral_credit metrics
- run synthetic churn test (bursty pattern) against canary

frank: Also add a safety: if a node-level overload happens, operator may preempt ephemeral_credit consumers before committed tenants. Priority enforcement must be explicit.

carla: Agreed — preemption policy: committed > reserved_burst > ephemeral_bank in that order. We'll document preemption signals.

alice: Action items:
- carla: draft operator contract doc (control-plane signals + allowed local stabilizers) — due EOD tomorrow
- ben: add metrics (scale_decision_reason, ephemeral_credit) to canary telemetry — today
- esha: run synthetic churn harness once metrics in — tomorrow morning
- frank: stub preemption enforcement in operator (config flag) — this week

carla: Got it. I'll start the doc and paste a minimal state diagram in the doc.

ben: I'll hook up the telemetry and post a small dashboard.

alice: Thanks all. If anyone finds a repro, drop logs here and ping @alice. :thumbsup:

frank: quick note — we should cap ephemeral_credit total cluster-wide to avoid headroom explosion. Maybe a global ephemeral_budget_ratio metric.

esha: Good call. Add to checklist.

alice: End of sync. Short follow-up thread tomorrow after canary metrics.
